citeAs: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li (2025). VoiceAssistant-Eval: Benchmarking AI Assistants Across Listening, Speaking, and Viewing. arXiv:2509.22651.
creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li (CUHK MMLab, SenseTime Research, CPII under InnoHK)
description: VoiceAssistant-Eval is a comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing. It comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories, including natural sounds, music, spoken dialogue, multi-turn dialogue, role-play imitation, and highly heterogeneous images. The benchmark is the first to provide a comprehensive quantitative and qualitative evaluation of AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing abilities.
name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluation validation was conducted on 10% of Qwen2.5-Omni-7B's responses (1,050 examples across 13 tasks). Pearson correlation coefficients between automated (gpt-oss-20b) and human evaluations ranged from 0.73 to 1.00, with an overall correlation of 0.92. Agreement rates were uniformly high (often above 90%), with an overall agreement rate of 96.1%. Evaluation stability was assessed by repeating scoring 10 times on 1,050 examples, showing narrow variance (standard deviations mostly below 3). Statistical significance testing using paired two-sided t-tests with Bonferroni correction was also performed.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom lightweight web-based curation tool built by the authors, which ingests candidate items with metadata, raw prompts, reference answers, and associated media (audio, images, transcripts), and allows curators to assign Good/Bad verdicts with optional notes.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A multi-stage curation process was used: (1) Deduplication using lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance to flag potential duplicates, which were manually reviewed and removed; (2) Validation to exclude incomplete or unsuitable instances (corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, incorrect answers) — approximately 10% of candidates were discarded; (3) Categorization assigning problems to 13 predefined task categories based on source metadata; (4) Sampling to balance the ratio of different tasks. A web-based curation tool was used for manual review in three passes: media integrity, task well-posedness, and answer validity.
rai:dataBiases: The paper acknowledges several biases: (1) Monolingual focus — all prompts and evaluations are in English except five Chinese roles in the role-play task, which may not capture full variability of real user interactions; (2) The role-play subset uses a fixed set of 100 roles that may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas; (3) Questions and contexts are drawn from academic or synthetic sources, which might not reflect the full richness or fairness concerns of real deployments; (4) Automated GPT-based scoring may introduce noise and bias, potentially favoring certain phrasings.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from 47 source datasets spanning audio and visual modalities. For Listening, source data was drawn from 23 audio understanding datasets covering speech, sound, music, and general audio. For Speaking, data came from 22 datasets including 11 text datasets and 11 audio datasets, with role-play profiles from RoleBench. For Viewing, MMMU was used as the source dataset, spanning 30 disciplines and 30 image formats. Text instructions were converted to audio using TTS models. 100 distinct roles were selected with 3 representative audio clips per role.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data was drawn from 47 source datasets including audio datasets (LibriSpeech, Common Voice, Clotho, AudioCaps, AVQA, MusicCaps, MUSIC-AVQA, VocalBench, SD-Eval, VoiceBench, MEAD, RAVDESS, FMA, etc.) and text datasets (AlpacaEval, RoleBench, AdvBench, BeaverTails-Eval, MT-Bench-101, IFEval, BIG-Bench Hard, FollowBench, CommonsenseQA, GSM8K, etc.), plus MMMU for visual content. A total of 10 datasets for Speech, 6 for Sound, 4 for Music, and 3 for General listening were used.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include: (1) Monolingual focus (primarily English) limiting generalizability to diverse linguistic settings; (2) Limited model evaluation scope (primarily open-source, only one proprietary system GPT-4o-Audio); (3) Reliance on automated measures and GPT-based scoring which may introduce noise and bias; (4) Potential biases from source data and design choices; (5) Gaps in task coverage — video-audio integration and continuous audio-visual streaming tasks are not included; (6) Static offline evaluation that does not measure latency, partial utterance handling, barge-in, or error recovery; (7) Dataset size (10.5K items) may still be limited in diversity.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: After curation, balanced sampling was applied to equalize category representation across the 13 task categories. 300 role audio clips from the role-play task were reused as prompt audio to increase speaker diversity during speech synthesis.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text preprocessing for TTS synthesis included: (1) replacing image reference tokens (e.g., "<image1>") with descriptive phrases; (2) rewriting text using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct to ensure numbers and mathematical expressions are read accurately; (3) rephrasing multiple-choice options for better readability. Speech synthesis used F5TTS, ChatTTS, and Dia-1.6B, with UTMOS Strong scoring to filter out clips below 3.8. Whisper-Large-v3 was used to transcribe synthesized audio, retaining only the sample with the lowest word error rate. In total, 13,471 high-quality speech audio files were synthesized.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark includes role-play voice imitation and speaker similarity evaluation, raising concerns about identity spoofing, harassment, and fraud. Safeguards include: (i) prohibiting training or releasing models intended to reproduce identifiable speakers without documented consent; (ii) requiring downstream users to implement consent gating and watermarking or traceability of synthetic audio; (iii) providing "safety cards" describing acceptable use, known risks, and red-team tests for voice cloning abuse. A data governance process for auditing and removal is maintained. The benchmark is intended to facilitate development of safer, more capable voice assistants across domains including healthcare, education, smart homes, and accessibility.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended for evaluating and benchmarking AI voice assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing capabilities. Specifically designed to assess: (1) audio understanding (natural sounds, music, speech); (2) voice personalization and speaker imitation; (3) hands-free voice interaction; (4) multimodal (audio+visual) integration; (5) safety alignment and robustness of voice assistants. Not intended for training models to cheat on the benchmark.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: F5TTS, ChatTTS, and Dia-1.6B (TTS models for speech synthesis); UTMOS Strong (MOS predictor for speech quality evaluation); Whisper-Large-v3 (ASR for transcription and WER computation); Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (text rewriting for TTS preprocessing); gpt-oss-20b (automated content quality evaluation); emotion2vec (emotion probability estimation); Wespeaker (speaker similarity computation for role-play evaluation)
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark includes role audio clips (300 clips from 100 roles, 3 clips per role) used for voice imitation tasks. Speaker similarity is evaluated using Wespeaker. The paper emphasizes strict consent, provenance, and anti-impersonation safeguards to mitigate misuse risks related to identity spoofing and privacy violations.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The paper does not specify a fixed number of independent annotations collected per item; curation involved manual review but no specific annotation count per item is stated.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: The paper does not describe the demographics of the human curators/annotators (expertise, nationality, language background, etc.).
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The paper does not specify when the data collection took place (start/end dates or period).
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not explicitly discuss missing data handling beyond filtering out corrupted/broken items during curation, which is covered under the annotation protocol.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: The paper does not describe any imputation protocol for missing or incomplete values.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper mentions a data governance process for auditing and removal but does not describe a formal versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan for the dataset.
